add.header: Domain subtrees for library, playback and player
add.description: services/library, services/playback, services/ffmpeg, widgets/player, widgets/glass and screens/settings each own one capability, so most changes stay inside one folder and a new engineer can find the owner by name.

add.header: Flat services/ catch-all
add.description: Top-level services/ mixes data services with UI glass and navigation state; the subtrees are the intended owners, and the flat files are historical accretion rather than a deliberate boundary.

add.header: Provider files consistently suffixed _provider
add.description: All 15 files in lib/providers end in _provider.dart, so a developer can locate and recognise a Riverpod provider from its filename alone.

add.header: services/library uses library_ module prefix
add.description: All 17 files in lib/services/library share a library_ prefix, which makes the persistence and collection group easy to scan and keeps its modules as separate libraries.

add.header: Record typedefs for request and result shapes
add.description: Providers and services use Dart record typedefs for request and result shapes, while entities live as classes in lib/models. The split is not documented; treat it as a neutral choice.

add.header: Part files invisible to dead-code scan
add.description: The dead_code detector flags part-split files as orphaned because it does not follow part directives. Treat those flags as a tooling blind spot.

add.header: Cleanup catches are deliberately tolerant
add.description: Empty catch blocks around staging, part-file and lease cleanup in backup_service and platform_bridge are intentional: a failed delete must not mask the primary result. They are not silent failures of user-visible work.

add.header: Handle-prefixed event handlers are idiomatic
add.description: _handleX and handleScroll names in widgets and the shell describe event handling in Flutter's usual way. They are not generic verbs that hide intent.

add.header: Query and predicate names match behaviour
add.description: getCount, getById, getCurrentPosition and getMediaItem are side-effect-free queries, and is/has predicates return bool. This is a consistent pattern in the data and playback layers.

add.header: Playback part-file collaborators share handler privates
add.description: AutoMix and Autoplay are real stateful helpers, but they receive the whole MusicPlayerHandler and read its private fields. The split is structural rather than a true boundary, so it hides coupling behind file separation.

add.header: Injected analyzer, renderer and loader seams
add.description: AutoMix analyzer and renderer and the Autoplay library loader are passed as typed constructor parameters, which keeps the heavy audio and database work replaceable in tests.

add.header: Every declared runtime package is directly imported
add.description: Each runtime dependency in pubspec.yaml has a direct package: import in lib/ or test/, and cupertino_icons backs CupertinoIcons used in sistrum_icons.dart. The manifest carries no dead runtime packages.

add.header: Exact pins and vendored audio forks
add.description: liquid_glass_easy, ffmpeg_kit_flutter_new_audio and material_color_utilities are pinned exactly, and audio_service plus audioplayers_android are vendored or overridden by path. These are deliberate but undocumented, so upgrade decisions depend on reading the manifest comments.

add.header: Paged queue store with typed cursor pages
add.description: LibraryDatabase.getQueueTrackPageResult returns QueueLibraryDbPage with a cursor, so artist and queue screens share one bounded paging seam over SQLite.

add.header: No snapshot or golden tests in the suite
add.description: The suite asserts behavior with widget and unit tests and does not rely on golden files. This keeps tests tied to behavior rather than rendered pixels.

add.header: Broad feature-level test coverage
add.description: About 284 test files span library, playback, settings, lyrics and glass UI. Most feature areas have at least one direct test file, which gives a developer a real safety net for feature changes.

add.header: Wall-clock polling helpers in widget tests
add.description: Several tests wait on DateTime.now() deadlines with real delays because platform file operations and event loops are not driven by the fake clock. The pattern is repeated and worth consolidating.

add.header: No accounts or backend, so no route auth
add.description: The app is a local/offline Android player with no user sessions, tokens or remote API. Auth-decorator and RLS concerns from the rubric do not apply, and the only remote call is the GitHub release check.

add.header: Exported Android components are standard entry points
add.description: Only the launcher activity, widget configuration, media browser service and media button receiver are exported. Internal receivers, the APK FileProvider and the background service are exported=false.

add.header: WHY-focused comments on concurrency and platform rules
add.description: Comments in local_library_provider and sqlite_helpers explain ordering, single-flight joins, trigram limits and SAF quirks. They describe constraints a new reader would otherwise miss.

add.header: Sparse logging, no entry/exit traces
add.description: debugPrint and AppLogger calls are limited to failure paths, so the log output stays signal rather than noise.

add.header: Guards concentrated at decode and file boundaries
add.description: Type and null checks in backup_service and collection restore codec sit on untrusted decoded JSON and file I/O, which is where they belong.

add.header: Scan notification try/catch duplication
add.description: Five scan notification methods repeat the same try/catch and differ only by callee and label. Known debt, candidate for one helper.

add.header: No deprecated symbols called in app sources
add.description: Deprecated markers appear only in vendored third_party packages. The app's lib/ and android/app sources contain no @deprecated usages or stale migration TODOs, so deprecation hygiene is consistent.

add.header: Persisted legacy identifiers kept deliberately
add.description: Legacy source ids and the legacy://local-library placeholder keep stored library rows and backups readable. They are encoded as named constants and are not migration residue.

add.header: Native backend and Dart fallback share platform flag
add.description: PlatformBridge.supportsCoreBackend (Platform.isAndroid) selects native implementations, while Dart implementations remain as else-branches for backup and collection reads. Those branches are reachable on device only through a row-count probe and in host tests.

add.header: Root entry files are genuine core
add.description: lib/app.dart and lib/main.dart at the lib root are the entry points with high fan-out and are correctly placed. The root is not a straggler problem.

add.header: Focused subpackages exist for library, playback, ffmpeg, glass and player
add.description: lib/services/library, lib/services/playback, lib/services/ffmpeg, lib/widgets/glass, lib/widgets/player and lib/widgets/audio_analysis show purpose-driven grouping that many files follow.

add.header: Part files are not orphans
add.description: music_player_automix.dart and music_player_autoplay.dart are included via part directives in music_player_service.dart. Orphan detection flags them falsely, so any cleanup should treat them as part of the service.

add.header: Domain-organized library and playback layers
add.description: Services, providers and library databases are organized by domain, and most large files hold one coherent concern. Mixed responsibilities concentrate in a few hotspots rather than spreading across the codebase.

add.header: Update checker keeps null distinct from unverified failure
add.description: checkForUpdate routes every release-list-dependent null through _throwUnverified, so a stale or unverifiable cache cannot be reported as up to date. The UpdateCheckException doc states this as the contract, which makes the rule explicit for callers.

add.header: Native edit responses decoded once into an enum
add.description: MetadataEditResult.decode turns the native channel map into MetadataEditOutcome and typed fields, so consumers never interpret protocol strings. This keeps the boundary typed and in one place.
